title: Choose the /design-system page structure
question: The Design Constitution fixes the world (WOVEN TRADE, brand green and signal amber, borders over shadows). This choice is how the page is organised. The roll dealt three structures; keep the lead, take another, or re-roll.

options.label: State Sheet
options.lineage: type-specimen sheets that show every weight at true size
options.thesis: Every component is documented as a matrix of its required and commerce states, rendered live at true size.
options.viewport: Green masthead with mode switch; layer index rail on the left; StatusBadge entry with its state sheet of ten required and ten commerce states.
options.risk: Large blocks make wide sheets; each entry shows only the states the spec names for it.

raised.raise: Every state carries a mark as well as a tone, so the sheet reads in greyscale and to screen readers.
Specimens keep true size; narrow screens drop state columns into rows, never shrink the component.

options.label: Build Order
options.lineage: technical manuals ordered by assembly sequence
options.thesis: The page follows the spec's nine build phases, tokens to marketing, on a thread rail that shows where you are.
options.viewport: Thread rail of nine phases across the top with phase 05 active; contents list on the left; ActionBar entry with live order-line actions and its dependencies in the margin.
options.risk: Finding one component means knowing its phase; the command palette has to carry lookup.

options.label: Trade Units
options.lineage: trade reference books organised by the goods they cover
options.thesis: Chapters follow the commercial units (product, stock, order, payment, shipment) and open with each unit's state thread.
options.viewport: Unit index on the left; Payment chapter opening with its SellaPay STK state thread; PaymentStatusPanel specimen awaiting M-Pesa confirmation.
options.risk: Generic fields and blocks belong to no unit and sink into an appendix; the index must not imply per-model components.

options.label: Cutting Bench Select Rail
options.thesis: Sections strung as frames on a perforated rail, set-asides hanging below.
options.viewport: A scrubbing frame strip across the sheet.
options.risk: Scrubbing a strip is a control readers must learn; docs need standard navigation.
options.case: Loses on clarity: component lookup is not a linear edit.
options.kept: State is a mark, not only a hue.

options.label: Sampler Alphabet Proof
options.thesis: Bands in order of difficulty, alphabets first, scene last.
options.risk: Literal textile would breach the constitution's no-skeuomorphism rule.
options.case: Its topology fuses into Build Order, which already holds it; adds nothing beyond.
options.kept: True-scale specimens; reflow by whole rows.

options.label: Hand-drawn Zine
options.thesis: Marker panels and mascots teach the system.
options.risk: Cream paper and marker is a model default and wrong for B2B trust.
options.case: Loses both axes: sellers and admins do not read their tools as comics.
options.kept: One highlighted line per example: the specimen's key value is marked.

options.label: Raygun Layout Desk
options.thesis: Colliding columns; reading order earned, not given.
options.viewport: Three overlapping headlines over a photograph.
options.risk: Breaks the reading order a reference must keep.
options.case: Loses both axes: operational docs need predictable lookup.
options.kept: Type scale with conviction in section openers.

options.label: Daylight Section
options.thesis: Rooms read along a moving edge of light.
options.viewport: One long continuous section with time stamps.
options.kept: Tabular time stamps on every event.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Weather cut into blocks and assembled.
options.kept: Measurements in a fixed-width face beside every block.
